name: Prize crossword No 23,681
preamble: For the purposes of this crossword, all numbers on the grid should be ignored.

clue.text: Victorian rogue to use poker on potential blaze at tea time

indicators.note: something potential is not yet in its final shape, so these letters still have to be arranged into one

blocks.note: to jab is to poke, as with a poker
taken as written, then rearranged
four o'clock is the traditional hour for afternoon tea

explanation.surface: A Victorian villain stokes a fire at tea time, poker in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Jabez Balfour was a Victorian MP and financier whose Liberator Building Society collapsed in 1892; he fled to Argentina and was jailed for fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Balfour was a notorious swindler of the 1890s, so he is a real nineteenth-century crook.

clue.text: Aristides - and there must be many others

definitions.text: Aristides - and there must be many others

blocks.note: surface: a single named figure from ancient Athens

blocks.clueFragment: and there must be many others
blocks.note: setter's reading: he was nicknamed for his fairness, and he is only one of many such people

explanation.walkthrough: Aristides the Just was an Athenian statesman famed for his fairness. Read his title as 'the just one', then as 'merely one of many', and both senses land.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a person noted for fairness and merely a single example among many.

clue.text: Listening to financial body's clever remarks is a treat

indicators.note: listening means attending to how words sound, not how they are written

blocks.note: a bank is a financial body, and wit is clever remarks

explanation.surface: Hearing the jokes of a bank's board is supposedly a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, BANK WIT sounds like the word for a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavish meal served to guests is a special indulgence, which is a treat.

clue.text: Code without one thing that transmits weak interaction

definitions.note: a relative clause standing in for the noun it describes

indicators.note: without means lacking, so something is taken away

blocks.note: a ZIP code is the American postal code
the Roman numeral one, removed
an article is an item or thing

explanation.surface: A program missing one feature that should pass along a faint signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Code' suggests computing, but it is the US postal code. The definition borrows 'thing' from the wordplay in spirit: the answer is the thing that transmits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Z boson is one of the carrier particles of the weak nuclear force in physics.

clue.text: Blend with something else 997 years ago

blocks.note: a date counted in years since Christ is marked AD, anno domini
the puzzle appeared in 2006, and 997 years earlier is 1009, which in Roman numerals is MIX

explanation.surface: A recipe step: mix in another ingredient, done centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Subtract 997 from the publication year 2006 to get 1009; write it as a date, AD plus the Roman numerals M and IX.
explanation.definitionFit: To admix is to add one substance into another so that they combine.

clue.text: Iron in itself contains carbon from fruit of tree

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another
to contain is to hold within, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: the metal itself, as its chemical symbol
taken as written
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A metallurgy note: iron with carbon in it, oddly sourced from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Itself' refers back to iron, so it means iron's own symbol FE; the word IRON, holding C, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody cone of a conifer carries its seeds, so it is the tree's fruiting body.

clue.text: Ulster's bond in US concerns time, place and action

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: taken as written, split to hold the rest
Ulster is commonly used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish financial bond issued in America, and what it covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests finance but is just a tie. The three classical unities are the rules for drama drawn from Aristotle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoclassical dramatic theory demanded unity of time, place and action, known collectively as the three unities.

clue.text: Victims of displacement activity enjoyed by Mr Squeers

blocks.note: first meaning: scapegoats who take blame shifted from others
second meaning, read literally: thrashing pupils, the favourite pastime of a cruel schoolmaster

explanation.walkthrough: Wackford Squeers is the brutal headmaster of Dotheboys Hall in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby. Displacement is the psychological shifting of anger onto a substitute target.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapegoats punished in place of the guilty, originally boys beaten instead of young princes, and literally the act of caning pupils.

clue.text: Houses for very little money, praise the Lord!

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house, so HOS for houses
an anna was a small Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: Cheap housing is cause for thanking heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The anna was a coin of British India, worth a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a biblical shout of adoration used in worship, an exclamation glorifying God.

clue.text: I get spoilt without getting spliced

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the damaged word sits round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
marred means spoilt

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being ruined by staying single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense meaning outside. Spliced is British slang for wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spliced is informal for joined in wedlock, as ropes are spliced together.

clue.text: Where castaway lies stranded, maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible version out of many, so the letters may be put another way

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A marooned sailor lying on a beach somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the letters of the two middle words rearrange to the answer, and the clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited isle is the classic place a shipwrecked person ends up marooned and alone.

clue.text: P-punishment with nasty cut as its yield

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so these letters are spoilt into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the stammered initial, taken as written
the rod is corporal punishment
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A stammering account of a beating that leaves a nasty wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'P-' is not just colour: it supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: What a process, farm or factory produces is its output, so product and yield are synonyms.

clue.text: "The Wrong Box" finishes with viral problems

indicators.note: wrong means incorrectly arranged, so these letters must be set in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to die is to finish

explanation.surface: The Wrong Box, a comic novel by Stevenson and later a film, ends with a viral illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a single unit, but 'Wrong' works on 'Box' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: X-bodies are inclusions seen in plant cells infected by certain viruses, so they are symptoms of viral disease.

clue.text: Incapable of moving from Berliner to tabloid?

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters come straight out of the run of words

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A newspaper unable to switch from the mid-sized Berliner format to tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: Berliner and tabloid are newspaper page sizes; the Guardian had just switched to Berliner when this appeared. The answer straddles the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something without power to move or act, lifeless and still.

clue.text: Study for the less intelligent can help store energy

definitions.note: describes the device rather than naming it

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
denser means more stupid

explanation.surface: A revision aid for weaker pupils that helps them keep their energy up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a noun but is the verb con. 'Can' looks like a container, yet it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is the older name for a capacitor, an electrical component that holds charge.

clue.text: The yield of the vine shall form US city

indicators.note: to form is to shape into something new, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding promise that the grape harvest will found a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The yield of the' only sets the scene; the anagram uses just the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville is the capital of Tennessee, famous as the home of country music.

clue.text: Hunters too, probably: there may be rags about

indicators.note: about means around and scattered, so these letters are moved round

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Huntsmen, it seems, leave scraps of cloth strewn around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the phrase hunter-gatherers: people who hunt are probably also the other thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Early foraging peoples are called hunter-gatherers, so those who hunt likely collect wild food as well.

clue.text: Old solver grasping about a US writer

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight, so one piece holds others inside

blocks.note: the solver is you, and thou is the old form of you
re means about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A veteran crossword solver tackling a clue about an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword clues often address the solver as 'you', so an old solver is the archaic thou.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden, was a nineteenth-century American essayist and naturalist.

clue.text: Look round at writer: he should keep an _____ on watch

definitions.text: he should keep an _____ on watch

blocks.note: to eye is to look at
O is round in shape
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A sentry should glance at the author and stay alert while guarding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the answer completes the saying in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep an eye open means to stay alert and vigilant, exactly what a sentry must do.

clue.text: Mongoose, one among kings (piece of Kipling)

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece sits inside another
a piece is only part, so just some letters are kept

blocks.note: R (rex) and K are both abbreviations for king
the Roman numeral one
the opening letter of the name
the next letter of the name

explanation.surface: A Kipling story about a mongoose, set among royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Rikki-Tikki-Tavi is the mongoose hero of Kipling's Jungle Book story; the parenthesis hints that the answer is only part of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name of Kipling's cobra-killing animal hero, the familiar form of Rikki-Tikki-Tavi.

clue.text: Greeting on appearances?

definitions.note: the answer is plural, as in 'send my regards'
in the old sense of looks or gazes

blocks.note: first meaning: good wishes sent to someone
second meaning: looks, as in steady gazes

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a hello prompted by how someone looks; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means kind wishes sent in a message and also looks or glances given.

clue.text: Playful country almost keeps Araucaria on the wagon

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to keep is to hold, so one piece holds others inside

blocks.note: Kenya is a country in East Africa
the setter refers to himself
TT is teetotal, and on the wagon means not drinking

explanation.surface: A frisky nation nearly persuades the setter to give up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the setter of this puzzle, so his name stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitteny means like a young cat, so frisky and fond of games.

clue.text: Gold I return to US city for mountain building

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
the ego is the self, the I
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A prospector heads back to an American city with gold for a building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not just one letter here: it is the Latin word for the self.
explanation.definitionFit: Orogeny is the geological process by which crustal folding raises ranges of peaks.

clue.text: Creature marked in portions 3 and 2 of Timothy

indicators.note: numbered portions point to particular parts of a word, taken in the stated order

blocks.note: the third portion when the name splits into three
the second portion of the same split

explanation.surface: A bookish note on an animal mentioned in parts of the Epistles to Timothy.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 and 2 of Timothy' sounds like Bible chapter references, but it means splitting the name as TI, MOTH, Y and taking parts three and two.
explanation.definitionFit: The Y-moth, or silver Y, has a pale Y-shaped mark on each forewing, so it is a marked insect.

clue.text: Meat about to achieve the un-meat-like

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: veal is calf meat
to get is to achieve

explanation.surface: Meat on the verge of becoming meatless.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer, which means unlike meat, is built round a meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetal means relating to plants, which are the opposite of animal flesh.

clue.text: Rag-and-bone man with small change going precipitately down into the water

definitions.text: going precipitately down into the water

indicators.note: a small change is a slight alteration, so the letters are moved around a little

blocks.note: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about a father and son who were rag-and-bone men, collectors of household junk

explanation.surface: A junk dealer with loose coins tumbling headlong into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small change' looks like coins, but it means a slight rearrangement: only two letters move.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep-to is a nautical term for a shore or bank that drops sharply into deep water.

clue.text: Like the Hydra, the eagle's in French for the year

blocks.note: the French article l' for 'the', followed by erne, a sea eagle
padding that gives no letters: it says 'the' and 'year' are to be put into French
an is French for year

explanation.surface: A mythological monster, a bird and a French date muddled together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In French' governs both 'the' and 'year'. The erne is a sea eagle, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles killed the many-headed Hydra at Lerna, so the monster is called Lernean.

clue.text: Heartless ruler's game keeping pupil at lycée unlettered so as not to be put out?

definitions.text: so as not to be put out?

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is taken out
to keep is to hold, so one piece holds another inside
stripped of letters, here the spelled-out name of a letter is cut away

blocks.note: a queen is a ruler
chess is a game
L for learner
a French secondary school; the deletion removes CÉE, which is how French spells the name of the letter C

explanation.surface: A monarch's chess game swallows a French schoolchild who can't read.
explanation.walkthrough: A lycée is a French secondary school. 'Unlettered' looks like illiterate, but it means removing a letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Quenchless means unable to be extinguished, so the adverb describes acting like a fire that cannot be doused.
